implementation: taehyun_paper_reproduction_nested — /Users/pig30nidae/Pig30nidaE/AJOU/26-1-summer/Google-AJOU-AI-Capstone/Taehyun/Paper_Reproduction_Nested/Cheon_LGBM.py (395 lines) + README.md (91 lines). A single script that builds a daily table from the AI-Hub CSVs, then runs four scenarios (Cheon_LGBM.py:382-387): S1 Leakage+SingleCV (record-level StratifiedKFold, SHAP forward selection on all data, Table-2 LightGBM), S2 Leakage+NestedCV (same + Optuna), S3 NoLeakage+SingleCV (StratifiedGroupKFold, per-fold SHAP forward selection, Table-2 LightGBM), S4 NoLeakage+NestedCV (S3 + Optuna inner tuning). Each scenario: 5 repeats x 5 folds (Cheon_LGBM.py:390, :276). It is a Cheon-derived LightGBM/SHAP-forward-selection pipeline, but with its own feature engineering (not the paper's 72 features), a date-join record construction, whole-dataset median imputation, and an Optuna tuner; only the LightGBM stage is covered (no 7-model Table 1 stage). All line references below are to Cheon_LGBM.py unless prefixed README.md.
cohort: Both AI-Hub partitions are read and pooled: train_activity.csv, val_activity.csv, train_sleep.csv, val_sleep.csv (:166-169), labels from training_label.csv / val_label.csv (fallback *_label_activity.csv) (:171-175), daily tables built per partition (:178-179) then concatenated (:181 `pd.concat([train_daily, val_daily])`). Label = DIAG_NM from the label CSV (:62-63), deduplicated per EMAIL (:64). No MMSE/cognitive-test file is read anywhere (grep for mmse/cognitive: none; only the label columns EMAIL/DIAG_NM are retained, :64). Subject count is neither asserted nor printed by the code; README.md:50 claims "Train 142명 + Validation 34명 = 총 176명", which contradicts the paper's 174 (PAPER_PROTOCOL Cohort) and ASSUMPTIONS A02 (141 + 33). Data path is Taehyun/data (:23-33), a separate copy from the repo's Data directory (not opened in this audit). Label merge is how="left" (:155), so any wearable subject missing from the label file would carry NaN label (see potential_errors).
record_count: Not printed to any saved artifact; only `X.shape` is printed at runtime (:380). README.md:37 says only "총 12,000+ 일치". The count arises from: activity.date = date of activity_day_start (:145); sleep.date = date of sleep_bedtime_end, i.e. wake-up date (:146); sleep rows sorted by (EMAIL, date, computed duration desc) and deduplicated to one row per (EMAIL, date) keeping the longest period (:148-151); inner merge on ["EMAIL","date"] (:153); train + val concatenated (:181). No row filtering afterwards (no dropna; NaNs are imputed, :187). Activity-side duplicates per (EMAIL, date) are not deduplicated, so the inner merge could multiply rows if any exist. By construction this cannot equal the paper's 12,183 (ASSUMPTIONS A03 reports that a wake-date join matches ~99.7 % of rows and leaves 12 duplicate sleep rows), so expect roughly 12.1k records with the shorter duplicate sleep periods discarded.
label: Code: binary_label_map = {"CN":0, "MCI":1, "Dem":1, "Dementia":1} (:61) -> CN vs MCI+Dem = 1, matching the paper (PAPER_PROTOCOL Classification task). A 3-class `original_label` (CN0/MCI1/Dem2, :60,:62) is also created but excluded from features (:184). However README.md:11 ("이진 분류 (CN vs MCI)") and README.md:52-54 ("Label 1: MCI") describe the task as CN vs MCI only, which does not match the code; the documentation is wrong, the code is paper-consistent. Positive class for ROC = 1 (predict_proba[:,1], :331; roc_auc_score(y_true, y_prob), :200).
record_construction: Date join, not row-wise pairing. Activity key = calendar date of activity_day_start (:140,:145); sleep key = calendar date of sleep_bedtime_end (wake-up date) (:143,:146). Duplicate sleep periods for the same (EMAIL, wake-date) are collapsed by keeping the one with the largest (bedtime_end - bedtime_start) (:148-151, `drop_duplicates(["EMAIL","date"], keep="first")`). Inner merge on (EMAIL, date) with suffixes ("", "_sleep") (:153). Label attached by left merge on EMAIL (:155). The paper implies row-wise pairing yielding 12,183 records (ASSUMPTIONS A03), and keeps sleep_period_id as a feature (multiple sleep periods per day retained); here the extra periods are dropped and ~0.3 % of days that do not date-match are lost. Timestamp columns and helper columns are dropped after feature building (:159-160).
missing_values: (1) All non-key columns coerced with pd.to_numeric(errors="coerce") (:46-53) -> non-numeric tokens become NaN. (2) +/-inf -> NaN (:161). (3) Column-median imputation fit on the ENTIRE pooled dataset (train+val partitions, all subjects, all future test folds) before any CV split: `all_daily[features] = all_daily[features].fillna(all_daily[features].median())` (:187). Nothing is refit inside folds; `run_scenario` receives the already-imputed X (:379,:390). Derived features can be NaN when a series is empty (ratios at :95,:112; stats at :83), and the sleep_hr_5min / sleep_rmssd_5min stats with remove_zero=True (:127,:129) can also be empty, so imputation is not vacuous here (unlike ASSUMPTIONS A13 where the 72 features have 0 NaN). README.md:67 claims sequences are parsed and missing values handled "각 Fold의 학습 단계에서" (inside each fold's training step); the code does it once globally (:157,:187). Paper reports no imputation method; whole-dataset median imputation is an unstated assumption and a (mild) train/test leak in the "Zero-Leakage" scenarios 3/4.
features: Feature list is not fixed: every numeric column of the merged table except EMAIL, original_label, label, DIAG_NM, date (:184-185), so it includes all raw numeric activity/sleep columns present in the CSVs (including columns the paper excluded, e.g. sleep_is_longest, sleep_temperature_deviation, if present) plus 57 derived columns. Exact count only printed at runtime (:380). Derived features: (a) activity_class_5min (:87-101): counts AND ratios for classes 0-5 (12), activity_rest_ratio, activity_inactive_ratio, activity_active_ratio (3+4+5), activity_not_worn_ratio, activity_class_valid_count = 17; -1 tokens removed (:89). Paper has only counts of classes 1-4. (b) activity_met_1min (:78-85, :125): mean, std, var, min, max, median, q25, q75, iqr, valid_count = 10; std/var via np.std/np.var => ddof=0 (population), quantiles via np.percentile default linear, median = np.median; -1 tokens removed (:80). ABSENT vs paper: kurtosis, skewness, autocorrelation, quantile_50 (no kurtosis type / autocorr lag exists at all). Extra: iqr, valid_count. (c) sleep_hr_5min stats (10, :127, remove_zero=True) - the paper explicitly REMOVED the 5-min heart-rate log (PAPER_PROTOCOL Preprocessing item 3). (d) sleep_rmssd_5min stats (10, :129) - not among the paper's 72. (e) sleep_hypnogram_5min (:103-115): sleep_{deep,light,rem,awake}_count_5min (= paper's hypnogram counts 1-4, renamed), the 4 ratios, sleep_stage_transition_count, sleep_hypnogram_valid_count = 10; tokens -1 and 0 filtered (:105). Paper features ABSENT: sleep_time (end-start; `_sleep_duration_seconds` is computed at :150 only for dedup and dropped at :159), sleep_bedtime_start and sleep_bedtime_end (no clock-to-real conversion; raw strings and datetime versions are dropped, :159), activity_met_1min_kurtosis/skewness/autocorrelation/quantile_50. Note sleep_bedtime_end (#4), activity_met_1min_kurtosis (#10) and activity_met_1min_autocorrelation (#20) are in the paper's Figure 6 top-20. No all-identical-column removal beyond the explicit timestamp drops (:159); no scaling.
feature_selection: `shap_forward_selection(X, y)` (:218-263). Ranking: StratifiedKFold(5, shuffle=True, random_state=42) on records (:222); per fold fit LGBMClassifier(n_estimators=100, random_state=42) (= library default trees) on the fold's training rows (:226-227), shap.TreeExplainer(model) default (tree_path_dependent) (:229), SHAP values computed on the same training rows X[tr] (:230), positive class if a list is returned (:231-232), importance = mean |SHAP| per feature, averaged over the 5 folds (:233-235), sorted descending (:236). Forward selection: features added one at a time in rank order (:243-245); each candidate set scored by 5-fold CV using the SAME kf splits (:247) with LGBMClassifier(n_estimators=50, random_state=42) (:248, non-default), fold-mean ROC-AUC (:253); best set = strict-improvement argmax (:254-256); early stop when 15 consecutive additions fail to improve (:259-260) - so the full path to all features is not evaluated and k is not fixed at the paper's 40; k printed only at runtime (:262). Where computed: Scenarios 1/2 (leakage_allowed=True): on ALL records once at repeat 0 and reused for repeats 1-4 (:281-283; comment :280). Scenarios 3/4: on the outer training fold only, per fold per repeat (:294-297), but the internal ranking/scoring CV is record-level StratifiedKFold (:222), not group-aware, so k is chosen by a subject-leaky criterion inside the training fold. SHAP is computed on the untuned 100-tree model, never on the Table-2 or Optuna model.
split: Outer: S1/S2 record-level StratifiedKFold(n_splits=5, shuffle=True, random_state=42+repeat) (:278-279); S3/S4 subject-level StratifiedGroupKFold(n_splits=5, shuffle=True, random_state=42+repeat) with groups = raw EMAIL (:285-286, :191). 5 repeats (n_repeats=5, :390; loop :276) -> seeds 42-46. No hold-out: the 33/34-subject Validation partition is pooled into the CV pool (:181). Nested: S2/S4 have an inner StratifiedKFold(n_splits=3, shuffle=True, random_state=42) inside each outer training fold for Optuna (:311-317) - record-level even in S4, so subjects are shared between inner train and inner validation. The SHAP forward-selection CV is likewise record-level StratifiedKFold(5, rs=42) in every scenario (:222,:247). In S1/S2 the FS splits (rs=42) are identical to the outer repeat-0 splits (rs=42+0) because StratifiedKFold depends only on y and random_state (:222 vs :278).
model_and_hyperparameters: LightGBM only (the paper's 7-model Table 1 stage is not reproduced). S1/S3 (use_nested_cv=False): LGBMClassifier(min_child_samples=41, num_leaves=330, n_estimators=1000, learning_rate=0.08, random_state=42, verbose=-1) (:328) = the paper's Table 2 values as fixed constants, no grid search, other params library default. S2/S4 (use_nested_cv=True): Optuna study (default TPE sampler, no sampler seed, :320), n_trials=10 (:321), space learning_rate log-uniform [0.01,0.3], num_leaves int [20,500], min_child_samples int [10,100] (:304-306), with n_estimators fixed at 150 during the search (:307) and inner objective = mean AUC over StratifiedKFold(3) (:311-318); the final model then uses best_params with n_estimators overwritten to 500 (:323-326). The paper's iterative grid search (num_leaves 100-1000 -> 220-380 -> 310-330) is not replicated. SHAP model: n_estimators=100 (:226); forward-selection path model: n_estimators=50 (:248). Threshold 0.5 (:332).
statistics: Per-fold metrics (accuracy, ROC-AUC, precision, recall, F1, sensitivity, specificity; :198-207) are appended to flat lists across all 5 repeats x 5 folds (:335-341) and summarised by `get_stats` (:209-216): mean, np.std (ddof=0), and a 95 % t-interval st.t.interval(0.95, n-1, loc=mean, scale=st.sem) with n = 25 pooled fold scores treated as independent (sem uses ddof=1, inconsistent with the reported +/-). No per-repeat (Figure-3 style) fold-mean is computed, contrary to ASSUMPTIONS A21. Precision/recall/F1 use sklearn default binary averaging on class 1 (:201-203), not macro. Threshold = 0.5 on predict_proba (:332). Confusion matrix is pooled over all 25 folds (each record counted 5 times) and saved as a heatmap (:343-344, :365-376).
reported_results: None. The script only prints to stdout (:356-363) and saves confusion-matrix PNGs to ./outputs/Cheon_LGBM_<scenario>.png (:366-375); no outputs/ directory, PNG, log or results table for this script exists in the repository (find over the repo excluding data dirs returned nothing), and neither README.md (Paper_Reproduction_Nested) nor Taehyun/README.md reports any AUC or accuracy for it (Taehyun/README.md:44 and :75 only describe/launch it). So no numbers can be attributed to any stage; the README's stated design is that Scenario 1 approximates the paper environment and Scenario 4 is the strict estimate (README.md:21-24).

potential_errors.description: Whole-dataset median imputation is fit on all records (both partitions, all subjects) before the CV split, so test-fold statistics enter the training data in the 'Zero-Leakage' scenarios 3/4; README claims this happens per fold.
potential_errors.evidence: Cheon_LGBM.py:187 `all_daily[features].fillna(all_daily[features].median())` executed in process_raw_to_daily_level before run_scenario (:379,:390); README.md:67

potential_errors.description: In Scenario 4 the inner hyperparameter CV is record-level StratifiedKFold(3), not group-aware, so the same subject appears in inner-train and inner-validation; the Optuna objective is subject-leaky and will favour memorising configurations (large num_leaves / small min_child_samples). Outer test subjects are still held out, but the 'nested subject-level' claim does not hold for the inner loop.
potential_errors.evidence: Cheon_LGBM.py:311 `inner_cv = StratifiedKFold(n_splits=3, shuffle=True, random_state=42)` used with X_tr/y_tr from the StratifiedGroupKFold outer fold (:285-286, :299)

potential_errors.description: The SHAP ranking and the forward-selection scoring CV inside shap_forward_selection are record-level StratifiedKFold even when called on the outer training fold in Scenarios 3/4, so k and the selected set are chosen by a subject-leaky criterion (tends to select many subject-identifying features and an optimistic k).
potential_errors.evidence: Cheon_LGBM.py:222 `kf = StratifiedKFold(n_splits=5, shuffle=True, random_state=42)`, used at :225 and :247; called with the group-split training fold at :295

potential_errors.description: In Scenarios 1/2 the forward-selection CV splits (rs=42) are identical to the outer repeat-0 test folds (rs=42+0) because StratifiedKFold splits depend only on y, n_samples and random_state; the feature subset is therefore chosen to maximise AUC on exactly the folds that are then reported as repeat-0 test performance (maximal optimism beyond ordinary 'select on all data' leakage).
Optuna study is created without a seeded sampler, so Scenario 2/4 results are non-reproducible run-to-run despite random_state=42 elsewhere.

Hyperparameters are tuned with n_estimators=150 but the final model is refit with n_estimators=500 and the tuned learning_rate/num_leaves; the selected configuration was never evaluated at 500 trees, so the refit can overfit (no early stopping).

The 95 % CI treats the 25 pooled fold scores (5 repeats of the same data) as independent samples (n=25) and the reported +/- uses population SD (np.std, ddof=0) while the CI uses sem (ddof=1); the CI is too narrow and the two dispersion numbers are inconsistent. The pooled confusion matrix counts every record 5 times.

Label merge is how='left' and y is cast with .astype(int) without dropping unlabeled rows; if any wearable subject is missing from the label file (README's 176 vs paper's 174 suggests an ID-set mismatch) the script raises on NaN->int, and if read_csv_flexible silently returns an empty label frame (:44) the 'label' column never exists (KeyError at :190). No assertion on subject/record counts exists.

Activity rows are not deduplicated per (EMAIL, date) before the inner merge, so duplicate activity days (if present in the CSVs) would be multiplied against the single kept sleep row; the resulting record count is never checked against the paper's 12,183.

Feature list includes every numeric raw column that survives the drop list, with no guard against identifier-like or constant columns (e.g. an index column or sleep_period_id after dedup); since the raw CSVs are not inspected here this is a risk, not a confirmed leak. Label-derived columns (DIAG_NM, original_label, label) and EMAIL are correctly excluded.

differences_vs_new_implementation: A02 (pooled partitions): same pooling (Cheon_LGBM.py:181), but README.md:50 claims 176 subjects vs A02's 141+33=174; no count assertion in code.

A03 (row-wise pairing -> 12,183 records): existing uses an inner date join on activity_day_start date = sleep_bedtime_end date with longest-period sleep dedup (:145-153), so the record set differs and shorter duplicate sleep periods are discarded.
A04 (label from DIAG_NM, MMSE never opened): same in substance (:62-64, :171-175); label file copy is training_label.csv / val_label.csv rather than the Gait copy.
A05 (hashed subject id): existing uses raw EMAIL directly as the CV group (:191); no effect on results, privacy differs.

A06/A07 (bedtime clock conversion; sleep_time = clock difference): existing has neither feature - bedtime columns are dropped (:159) and no sleep_time column exists (duration computed only for dedup at :150).

A08 (MET stats: pandas ddof=1 std/var, Fisher kurtosis, skew, autocorr lag 1, linear quantiles, median = q50 duplicate): existing uses np.std/np.var ddof=0 (:85), np.percentile linear (:84), removes -1 tokens (:80), has no kurtosis/skewness/autocorrelation, adds iqr and valid_count, and keeps only median (no q50 duplicate).

A09 (classes 1-4 and hypnogram 1-4 only; no HR/RMSSD logs): existing counts classes 0-5 plus ratios (:92-99), filters hypnogram tokens 0 and -1 and adds ratios/transition count (:103-115), and adds 20 features from the 5-min HR and RMSSD logs (:127,:129).

A10 (R: StratifiedKFold shuffle; G/N: StratifiedGroupKFold shuffle): same outer schemes (:278, :285) and same seeds 42-46 (A01/A24), but existing's inner CVs (SHAP FS :222; Optuna :311) are record-level StratifiedKFold, unlike A19's StratifiedGroupKFold inner loop.
A11 (macro precision/recall; 0.5 threshold): existing uses binary averaging on class 1 (:201-203); threshold 0.5 is the same (:332); adds sensitivity/specificity.
A12 (seven base models with library defaults): existing runs LightGBM only; no Table 1 stage.
A13 (no imputer, no scaler; 0 NaN): existing applies whole-dataset median imputation (:187) because its extra features can be NaN; no scaler (same).

A14 (TreeExplainer, mean |SHAP| positive class, explained on fitting rows, default LightGBM): same explainer and aggregation (:229-233), but averaged over 5 fold-models (:222-235) instead of a single model on all data.
A15 (R: ranking on all 12,183 records once per repeat): existing S1/S2 rank once at repeat 0 and reuse for all repeats (:281-283); FS splits coincide with repeat-0 outer folds (:222 vs :278).

A16 (default LightGBM along the path; k* = argmax over k=1..72, ties -> smallest k): existing scores the path with n_estimators=50 (:248), uses strict-improvement argmax with an early stop after 15 non-improving steps (:254-260), so the full path is not evaluated.
A17 (G: train-fold ranking with k fixed at 40): existing S3 searches k on the training fold with a record-level inner CV (:295, :222) instead of fixing k=40.
A18 (Table 2 constants in R and G): same for S1/S3 (:328).

A19/A20 (N: StratifiedGroupKFold(5) inner; 16-config grid of {default, Table-2} values; ranking on whole outer-train; k* from inner-mean AUC): existing S4 uses Optuna TPE 10 trials over a continuous space with StratifiedKFold(3) inner (:302-321), n_estimators 150 during search vs 500 final (:307, :323), and does FS once on the whole outer-train fold rather than inside the inner loop.
A21 (per-repeat fold mean, then mean/SD/t-CI across 5 repeats; pooled-fold as sensitivity only): existing reports only the pooled 25-fold mean, population SD and t-CI with n=25 (:209-216, :348-354).
A22/A23: existing also uses min_child_samples as the alias (:328); no environment/version file is provided.
A25/A26 (smoke run; run manifest; OOF files): existing has no smoke mode, no manifest, no saved OOF predictions or results files - only stdout and confusion-matrix PNGs (:356-376).
